## Solarum 0.10.0 – your own sounds, a Solari that listens, and a sturdier engine 🪐

> Solarum is still very much under development. Try it, break it, tell us what you think – criticism, ideas and help are very welcome: [open an issue](https://github.com/tj537/solarum/issues).

### Your own sounds
- **SOUNDS** on the start screen opens your sound library, out in deep space.
- **+ New sound** walks you through it step by step – *Start › Draw or Record › Finish* – with Cancel and Back always in the same place. **Draw** a sound on a drawing board (paint over a track's template, pen and eraser, a loudness lane, undo), **record** it with your microphone, or **import** a WAV, AIFF, MP3, FLAC or OGG file.
- The editor shows the sound as it will play: drag start, end and fades, change pitch, cut lows and highs, crush it, reverse it. Space plays it.
- Every sound belongs to one track. Pick it in that track's sound menu under *Your sounds*. A project can use up to 32 of them, and a saved project carries its sounds along, so it plays the same on another computer.

### More sounds, named for space
- **17 new built-in sounds** – kicks, claps, rims, hats, rides, basses, pad, organ and supersaw – 51 in all, with names like *Pulsar*, *Comet* and *Nebula*. Levels are balanced so switching sounds doesn't jump in volume.

### Solari listens
- **Every change is picked by ear.** Solari tries several changes on a copy of the groove and plays the one that sounds best right now.
- **It learns your taste.** A thumb up keeps a change and Solari does more of that; a thumb down puts it back and Solari does less of it.
- **SOLAR OS shows the cycle ahead** as a curve: where the breakdown comes and when the drop lands.
- **One ENERGY slider** from *CHILL* to *TURN UP* (also `chill` and `turnup` in the terminal).
- **Solari's manual:** `help` lists every command by topic – click one to run it. `seed <word>` rolls the same beat for the same word, every time.
- **PICK A GENRE** in SOLAR OS's menu; **SHUFFLE** rolls every track that's on.

### By hand means by hand
- With SOLAR OS off, Solarum plays exactly what you programmed and changes nothing by itself.
- Everything SOLAR OS does, you can do by hand with a right-click.

### Live
- **Tape stop** spins back up onto the beat when you let go. **Crush** fades one lo-fi sound in and out. The gate sounds the same at any sample rate.
- The **filter pad** looks like what it does: low-pass on one side, high-pass on the other, the puck on a rubber band back to the middle.
- The master EQ is capped at ±5 dB, so it can't wreck the mix.

### Sturdier and safer
- **Projects from other people are checked before they play:** oversized files are refused, packed sounds are limited to 30 seconds each, and every value is repaired. A broken sound can no longer silence the whole engine – if anything goes wrong in the audio, Solarum goes quiet for a moment and restarts it.
- **Saving never leaves half a file.** Projects, recordings and your sound library are written to a temporary file first and then swapped in, so a crash or a full disk can't break them.
- Recording from the microphone no longer stalls the input while the waveform is drawn.
- The audio callback never asks for memory, whatever buffer size your sound card picks.
- Broken MIDI messages are ignored instead of transposing by nonsense.

### Around the app
- A website: **[tj537.github.io/solarum](https://tj537.github.io/solarum/)**, with downloads and first-launch guides.
- Third-party licenses ship with the app. There's a contributing guide, a code of conduct and a security policy with private reporting.
- Under the hood: the UI code is split into smaller modules, GitHub Actions are pinned to commits, Dependabot keeps them current, and every build is checked for known vulnerabilities (`cargo deny`). Building it yourself needs Rust 1.96 or newer.

### Downloads

- **macOS 11+** (Apple Silicon & Intel): `Solarum-macos-universal.zip`
- **Windows 10/11:** `Solarum-windows-x64.zip`

Check them against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

The Mac app is not notarized yet: on first launch, open *System Settings → Privacy & Security* and click *Open Anyway*. Windows SmartScreen may ask once: *More info → Run anyway*.
